Egalitarian

ih-gal-ih-TAIR-ee-un -- five syllables, stress on TAIR. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Egalitarian is relating to the belief that all people deserve equal rights and treatment.

The founders designed an egalitarian classroom where every student, regardless of background, had the same voice in discussions.

Worked Example

At the new company, the intern and the chief executive eat at the same tables, receive the same benefits, and cast equal votes on office policy.

A workplace built on the principle that everyone deserves the same rights and treatment is egalitarian. The word describes a belief or system committed to equality -- not just a single act of fairness in one moment.

How Egalitarian Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

equitable

equitable: fair and even-handed toward everyone

unbiased

unbiased: free of favoritism or prejudice

democratic

democratic: giving every member an equal say

Antonyms

elitist

elitist: believing a select few deserve special status or treatment

discriminatory

discriminatory: treating certain people or groups unfairly

How Strong Is It? — unbiased → democratic → egalitarian

unbiased vs. egalitarian

unbiased vs. egalitarian: Unbiased is smaller in scope than egalitarian -- a single referee can be unbiased in one game, while egalitarian names a whole principled commitment that all people deserve equal rights and treatment.

democratic vs. egalitarian

democratic vs. egalitarian: Democratic can reach even further than egalitarian: an egalitarian outlook holds that everyone deserves equal treatment, while a fully democratic system builds that belief into its very structure, giving every member an equal voice in every decision.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — egal-/equ-

root — egal-/equ-: equal, level (French egal, from Latin aequus)

suffix — -arian

suffix — -arian: believing in, advocating (Latin -arius)

Put it together

Put it together: Egalitarian builds on French egal ('equal'), from Latin aequus ('equal, level'), plus -arian ('believing in'). An egalitarian person or system, at the root, is one that believes in the level field -- equal rights and equal treatment for all.

Use the root in a new word: equator

Use the root in a new word: equator: The ship crossed the equator at midnight, passing from the Northern Hemisphere into the Southern.

Root Check

Word Choice

Egalitarian describes beliefs, systems, and societies committed to equal rights: an egalitarian policy, an egalitarian constitution, an egalitarian marriage. Do not use it as a fancy word for 'nice' or 'fair' in a single moment -- it names a principle of equality, not one kind gesture.
